title: What if humans never needed sleep?
sources: Harvard Medical School Division of Sleep Medicine

lines.text: Humans spend roughly one third of their entire lives unconscious in bed.
lines.caps: Humans spend *one-third | of their life | in *bed

lines.text: What if we were biologically engineered to operate twenty-four-seven without ever needing sleep?
You would suddenly gain an extra eight hours of waking life every single day.
lines.caps: You gain *eight extra | hours every single | *day!

lines.text: Scientific discovery, arts, and personal hobbies could advance at twice the speed of human history.
However, corporate culture might immediately expand standard work days from eight hours to sixteen.
Energy consumption would double, and the soothing mental reset of dreams would disappear forever.
Would you give up sweet dreams and cozy blankets for eight extra working hours?
lines.caps: Would you trade *sleep | for extra hours? | Let us *know!
